name: Edwin Najmi Submission Attack System
description: Explore Edwin Najmi submission entries through Darce, triangle and Estima-lock study tracks, with specific course guidance and practical positional checkpoints.
summary: The Edwin Najmi Submission Attack System is a BJJGraph study guide for recognising Darce, triangle and Estima-lock opportunities within distinct positional exchanges.
overview:
Mission Submission groups Edwin Najmi's instruction into Darce, triangle and Estima-lock sections. The listed setups span top and bottom positions, with gi-dependent guard entries alongside techniques that do not require fabric grips. This makes the course a set of specialised attacking tracks rather than one universal chain.

BJJGraph's original plan below starts with the Darce track and adds a second family only when it fits the student's existing positions. The useful question is whether an opportunity appears during movement and can be converted into recognisable control. Submission-oriented study still needs positional judgement; a possible grip is not a reason to abandon a stable position or force an unfamiliar finish.
key_principles: Choose one submission family before combining the course tracks.
Recognise the positional opening before committing to the attacking grip.
Keep gi-dependent setups separate from no-gi practice choices.
Compare a top and bottom entry by the control available afterward.
Treat Estima-lock control as a separate advanced study topic.
Use grounded triangle entries before considering more dynamic variations.

key_components.description: Compare a side-control entry with a half-guard entry and identify the head-and-arm relationship each requires.
key_components.purpose: Give the first study track a concrete positional focus.

key_components.description: Select a familiar grounded guard entry and note whether sleeve grips or other fabric controls are part of the setup.
key_components.purpose: Match the chosen entry to the equipment and game being practised.

key_components.description: Study where the foot becomes accessible in a selected passing exchange without attempting a surprise application.
key_components.purpose: Separate spotting the opportunity from executing an advanced lock.

key_components.description: Assess whether pursuing the chosen submission preserves control or makes a pass, reversal or escape easier for the partner.
key_components.purpose: Keep the attacking objective connected to positional consequences.

implementation_sequence.description: Study one top side-control setup and end practice at a recognisable head-and-arm control position.
Use the matching half-guard lesson to identify what changes in access, available space and balance.
Choose a closed-guard or other familiar grounded entry. Note which grips are essential before trying it without the gi.
With a coach, use one leg-drag context to identify the offered foot and a clear catch-and-release endpoint. Do not combine it with an uncontrolled passing round.
In a short positional exchange, name the attack that appeared and the position that would be surrendered to pursue it. Reset if the tradeoff is unclear.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The three submission tracks become a disconnected move list.
common_obstacles.solution: Start with the family that already appears in your rounds and delay the others.

common_obstacles.obstacle: A gi setup is attempted after removing its essential grip.
common_obstacles.solution: Record fabric dependence and select a different demonstrated entry when appropriate.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The attacker abandons a useful pass for a loose submission grip.
common_obstacles.solution: Compare the likely positional result with the control actually available.

common_obstacles.obstacle: An advanced foot-lock attempt surprises the partner.
common_obstacles.solution: Use a separate coached recognition drill with an agreed catch-and-release endpoint.

assessment_metrics.description: Describe what differs between the chosen side-control and half-guard starts.
Check whether the selected triangle setup fits the practice context.
Review recognition of the selected Estima-lock entry without pressure.
Assess the cost of pursuing an attack during movement.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph suggests two separate Darce entry rounds: one from side control and one from half guard. Stop at head-and-arm control and compare the available space. Add a grounded triangle track later. Keep Estima-lock recognition in a separate coached catch-and-release exercise so the opportunity can be discussed without a surprise joint-lock application.

progression_path.focus: Recognise one side-control entry without finishing pressure.
Study how half guard changes the same head-and-arm task.
Choose one grounded triangle that fits the available grips.
Recognise a submission opportunity and evaluate its positional cost.

common_mistakes: Trying to connect every course technique into one chain.
Ignoring the fabric grips used by a selected guard entry.
Confusing spotting an Estima-lock opportunity with readiness to apply it.

flashcards.question: Why begin Mission Submission study with one attacking track?
flashcards.answer: Darce, triangle and Estima-lock entries arise in different exchanges; choosing one familiar track makes the practice objective clearer.

flashcards.question: What should be compared between side-control and half-guard Darce entries?
flashcards.answer: Compare access to the head-and-arm relationship, available space and balance before assuming the same entry works unchanged.

flashcards.question: Why record the fabric grips in a triangle setup?
flashcards.answer: Some course entries rely on gi controls, so removing those grips changes the setup and may require choosing a different entry.

flashcards.question: How should an Estima-lock entry first be studied?
flashcards.answer: Use a separate coached recognition and catch-and-release exercise with an agreed endpoint, rather than surprising a partner during passing.

flashcards.question: What decision accompanies a submission opportunity during a pass?
flashcards.answer: Evaluate whether the available control justifies pursuing the attack and which positional advantage would be surrendered to do so.

flashcards.question: Why use grounded triangle entries early in this plan?
flashcards.answer: A familiar grounded context makes the grip and control problems easier to study before adding the demands of more dynamic entries.

products.title: Mission Submission
products.blurb: Three specialised submission tracks: Darce entries, triangle setups and Estima-lock opportunities.
products.best_for: Experienced students seeking focused attacking options; the course mixes gi-specific setups and advanced submissions rather than providing a beginner curriculum.
products.study_focus: Start with the Darce section and compare side-control and half-guard entries before selecting a second track.
products.practice_tip: BJJGraph suggestion: stop each Darce entry at control and record whether pursuing it improved or weakened your position.
